faq.q: What is a cinematic product video template?
faq.a: A ready scene for one product photo, with a light you choose and a slow camera move. You add the photo, a voice, captions, and background music. The clip opens like a short film.

faq.q: How do I make the film?
faq.a: Upload a sharp photo, or paste a product link. Name the surface, one light, and one camera move. Pick a size and a length. Then add sound in the editor and download.

faq.q: Why start from a photo instead of a film crew?
faq.a: The set, the light, and the camera move are made from the photo you already have. You skip the crew, the rental, and a new shoot.
Shops that sell a product with a clear shape or finish, such as speakers, bottles, lamps, watches, or sunglasses. Use it when you want a polished opening for a page or an ad.

faq.q: Can I do this on the first try?
faq.a: Start with a sharp photo that shows the whole product. Name one move, such as moving closer or sliding along the side. Check the edge before you post.
A sharp photo with the full product in the frame and clear edges, so it stands out from the background. A public product link works when that page already shows the photo.

faq.q: Which size and length can I pick?
faq.a: Each video uses one size: tall 9:16, square 1:1, wide 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4. 4:3 is a shorter wide size, and 3:4 is a little taller than a square. Make a wide 16:9 file for a page, and a tall 9:16 file for a phone post. Those are two files from the same photo. Lengths are 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. You see the credit cost before it starts.
A clip uses 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, and 120 for 30. Credits are the balance on your monthly plan. If the clip fails, those credits come back. Plans start at $24.50 a month.

faq.q: Does the clip include a voice, music, or my logo?
faq.a: You can add an AI voice, captions, and a track from the music library in the built-in editor. A logo already printed on the product photo stays part of that photo. The clip does not add a new logo.

faq.q: Can I run the file in ads?
faq.a: Yes. The download has no AIVideosUGC watermark, so our name is not stamped on the file. It can run on your site and in paid ads. You can also send it to TikTok, or to Meta (Facebook and Instagram), from your account. Check shiny shots for glare before you post. The clip is your ad, not a customer quote.

faq.q: Can I make several products, or use the API?
faq.a: Yes. Reuse the same light for a set of photos. That is a batch. You can switch the spoken line to another language. The API lets your own software send the photos. Each one shows its credit cost first.
